01

“that which God gives good tidings of to His servants”

An explanation transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 42:23).

864
Explanation from Sufyān No. 864: 1: 18

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
864: 1:18. Sufyan:
"that which God gives good tidings of to His servants" [read] with a lightened [verb] (verse 23).
العربية
864: 1: 18 سفيان الذي يبشر الله عباده مخففة (الآية 23) .

02

“And whatever misfortune befalls you is for what your hands have…”

An explanation transmitted from al-Ḥasan (Q 42:30).

865
Explanation from al-Ḥasan No. 865: 1: 5

al-Ḥasan

English
Transmission wording
865: 1:5. Sufyan, from Ismail al-Makki, from al-Hasan, on His words
"And whatever misfortune befalls you is for what your hands have earned": He said, there is no scratch from a twig, no stumble of the foot, and no twitch of a vein but that it is for a sin, and what God pardons us is more. Then he recited "And whatever misfortune befalls you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much" (verse 30).
العربية
865: 1: 5 سفيان عن اسمعيل الْمَكِّيِّ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ فِي قَوْلِهِ وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كسبت أيديكم قَالَ مَا مِنْ خَدْشِ عُودٍ وَلَا عَثْرَةِ قَدَمٍ وَلَا اخْتِلَاجِ عِرْقٍ إِلَّا هُوَ بِذَنْبٍ وَمَا يعفوا اللَّهُ عَنَّا أَكْثَرُ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كسبت أيديكم ويعفوا عن كثير (الآية 30) .

03

“and those who, when tyranny strikes them, defend themselves”

An explanation transmitted from Ibrāhīm (Q 42:39).

866
Explanation from Ibrāhīm No. 866: 2: 6

Ibrāhīm

English
Transmission wording
866: 2:6. Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, on His words
"and those who, when tyranny strikes them, defend themselves": He said, they disliked to be humiliated (verse 39).
العربية
866: 2: 6 عن سُفْيَانُ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي قَوْلِهِ وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَهُمُ البغي هم ينتصرون قَالَ كَانُوا يَكْرَهُونَ أَنْ يُسْتَذَلُّوا (الآية 39) .
Edition record 371507 · p. 268Link to report ↗
04

“It is not for any human that God should speak to him except by…”

Three explanations transmitted from Mujāhid ibn Jabr (Q 42:51).

867
Explanation from Mujāhid No. 867: 3: 1

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
867: 3:1. Sufyan, from Isa, from Mujahid:
"It is not for any human that God should speak to him except by revelation": He said, revelation is something cast into their hearts (verse 51).
العربية
867: 3: 1 سفيان عن عيسى بن مُجَاهِدٍ وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْيًا قَالَ الوحي شئ يقذف في قلوبهم (الآية 51) .
Edition record 371508 · p. 269Link to report ↗
868
Report from Mujāhid No. 868: 4: 2

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
868: 4:2. Sufyan, from Isa, from Mujahid:
"or from behind a veil": He said, Moses, peace be upon him.
العربية
868: 4: 2 سفيان عَنْ عِيسَى عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ أَوْ من وراء حجاب قَالَ مُوسَى ﷺ.
Edition record 371508 · p. 269Link to report ↗
869
Report from Mujāhid No. 869: 5: 3

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
869: 5:3. Sufyan, from Isa, from Mujahid:
"or He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills": He said, Gabriel to Muhammad, peace be upon him, and to the prophets, peace be upon them.
العربية
869: 5: 3 سفيان عَنْ عِيسَى عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولا فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ مَا يشاء قَالَ جِبْرِيلُ إِلَى مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ وَإِلَى النَّبِيِّينَ عليهم السلام

05

“and indeed you guide to a straight path”

An explanation transmitted from Mujāhid ibn Jabr (Q 42:52).

870
Explanation from Mujāhid No. 870: 6: 4

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
870: 6:4. Sufyan, from Isa, from Mujahid:
"and indeed you guide to a straight path": He said, you call (verse 52).
العربية
870: 6: 4 سفيان عَنْ عِيسَى عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ وَإِنَّكَ لتهدي الى صراط مستقيم قال تدعوا (الآية 52) .
